mainTopic: בית רבי's leniencies, and benefiting from a גוי's מלאכה on שבת: the משנה, the 'knows him' limit, and אביי and רבא on רבן גמליאל's ramp
overview: The amud opens by finishing a series of reports by רבי אבא בר כהנא in the name of רבי חנינא about leniencies for בית רבי. Their קרונות may be moved on שבת, even large ones 'like those in your father's house.' Their wine, sent in a גוי's wagons with only one חותם, was permitted, though he is unsure whether this follows רבי אליעזר or comes from fear of the נשיא. A new משנה teaches that a Jew may benefit from a מלאכה a גוי did for himself, but not from one done for the Jew, with examples of a lamp, water and a ramp, and a story about רבן גמליאל. The גמרא explains why each case is needed. Then a ברייתא adds that the היתר applies only when the גוי does not know the Jew. That limit seems to clash with רבן גמליאל on the ship. אביי answers that the ramp was not made in front of him, while רבא says a ramp, like a lamp, serves a hundred as easily as one. Two more ברייתות, about a bathhouse and a lamp at a banquet, are answered by saying that a service for a group is done with the majority in mind, and that last answer finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: Answer: Like the ones in your father's house
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר כהנא answers רבי זירא's question about an earlier item of בית רבי by comparing it to the ones in רבי זירא's father's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Like the ones of your father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the previous discussion from the last daf. רבי זירא had asked whether a certain item of בית רבי was carried by one person or by two. רבי אבא בר כהנא answers: 'like the ones in your father's house.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not give a number. He points to a familiar example. According to תוספות, it means the large ones, which still may be moved.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי אבא בר כהנא answers רבי זירא.

phrases.english: Like those of your father's house.
phrases.notes: According to תוספות, these are the large ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּאוֹתָן שֶׁל בֵּית אָבִיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question from the previous daf.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The item is like the large ones in רבי זירא's father's house.

steps.title: The קרונות of בית רבי may be moved on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר כהנא quotes רבי חנינא: the קרונות of בית רבי may be moved on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבא בר כהנא said in the name of רבי חנינא: The carriages of the house of רבי may be moved on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling begins. The sedan chairs or carriages used by בית רבי are not מוקצה and may be moved on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think something this big and heavy is like a fixed structure that may not be moved. The ruling treats it as a regular movable כלי. The next step will ask how big these carriages are.

keyTerms.meaning: It is permitted to move them
The household of רבי יהודה הנשיא

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said
Rabbi Ḥanina said:
The carriages of the house of Rabbi
phrases.notes: Sedan chairs used for carrying people.

phrases.english: may be moved on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling about בית רבי, in the same chain of statements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קרונות of בית רבי may be moved on שבת.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks how big the carriages are
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks whether these carriages are carried by one person or need two people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to him: Are these ones carried by one person, or by two people?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks a clarifying question to set the limits of the ruling. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Size matters here. Something so heavy that it needs two people might be considered too big to count as a movable כלי. He wants to know how far the היתר goes.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to him:
Ones that are carried by one person
or by two people?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: בְּנִיטָּלִין בְּאָדָם אֶחָד אוֹ בִּשְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the size limit of the ruling in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the היתר apply to carriages carried by one person, or also to ones that need two?

steps.title: Answer: Like the ones in your father's house
steps.stepSummary: The same answer is given: the carriages are like those in רבי זירא's father's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Like the ones of your father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר כהנא answers with the same words he used in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the large carriages in רבי זירא's family home as the example (as explained by תוספות). This means even large ones that need two people may be moved.
steps.whatToRemember: The קרונות of בית רבי may be moved on שבת, even the large ones.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Like those of your father's house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּאוֹתָן שֶׁל בֵּית אָבִיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Like the large ones in רבי זירא's father's house.

steps.title: רבי חנינא allows wine sent in a gentile's wagons with one seal
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא allowed בית רבי to drink wine carried in a גוי's wagons, even though it had only one seal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבא בר כהנא said: רבי חנינא permitted the household of רבי to drink wine carried in the wagons of a גוי, with one seal.
steps.whatsHappening: A new leniency for בית רבי is reported. Wine sent with a גוי, protected by only one seal, was allowed to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally there is a worry that the גוי opened the wine and poured it for עבודה זרה or touched it. That would make it יין נסך. In general, two seals are needed. Here one seal was enough.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said:

phrases.aramaic: הִתִּיר לָהֶם רַבִּי חֲנִינָא לְבֵית רַבִּי
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina permitted the household of Rabbi
to drink wine carried in the wagons of a gentile,
with one seal,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא: הִתִּיר לָהֶם רַבִּי חֲנִינָא לְבֵית רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another report about בית רבי, now about wine instead of מוקצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine sealed with one חותם and sent in a גוי's wagons was allowed to בית רבי.

steps.title: Unsure why: רבי אליעזר's view, or fear of the נשיא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר כהנא admits he does not know the reason. Either רבי חנינא holds like רבי אליעזר that one seal is enough, or the גוי was afraid of the נשיא's household.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I do not know whether it is because he holds like רבי אליעזר, or because of fear of the house of the נשיא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר כהנא offers two possible reasons for the ruling and leaves it unresolved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the first reason, one seal is always enough, which is a general rule. Under the second reason, it is a special case: the גוי would not dare tamper with the נשיא's wine. Otherwise two seals would still be needed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This decides whether the היתר is a general rule for everyone or applies only to the נשיא's house.
steps.whatToRemember: The one-seal היתר could be a general rule (following רבי אליעזר) or just a special case (fear of the נשיא). It is left unresolved.

phrases.english: And I do not know

phrases.aramaic: אִי מִשּׁוּם דְּסָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר,
phrases.english: whether it is because he holds like Rabbi Eliezer,
phrases.notes: Who holds that one seal is enough.

phrases.english: or because of the fear of the house of the Nasi.
phrases.notes: The גוי would not dare open it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא יָדַעְנָא אִי מִשּׁוּם דְּסָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same speaker adds that he is unsure of the reason behind the ruling in step 5. He gives two possibilities and does not settle between them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the היתר a general rule or a special case for the נשיא?

steps.title: משנה: Using a lamp lit by a gentile
steps.stepSummary: If a גוי lit a lamp for himself, a Jew may use its light. If he lit it for the Jew, it is אסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A גוי who lit a lamp: a Jew may use its light. But if it was lit for the Jew, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with the basic rule: what a גוי does on שבת for himself, a Jew may benefit from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It all depends on who the מלאכה was done for. If it was done for the Jew, חכמים forbade benefiting from it. This prevents a Jew from relying on a גוי to do מלאכה for him.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of a Jew

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A gentile who lit a lamp —
a Jew may use its light.
And if it was for a Jew — it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוֹי שֶׁהִדְלִיק אֶת הַנֵּר מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ לְאוֹרוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew may benefit from a גוי's מלאכה done for the גוי himself, but not from one done for the Jew.

steps.title: משנה: Water drawn by a gentile for his animal
steps.stepSummary: If a גוי drew water for his own animal, a Jew may water his animal after him. If it was drawn for the Jew, it is אסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he filled water to give his animal to drink, a Jew may give his animal to drink after him. But if it was for the Jew, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second example of the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גוי carried water from a public well. The same line applies: if he did it for himself it is מותר, and if he did it for the Jew it is אסור.

keyTerms.meaning: To give his animal to drink

phrases.english: If he filled water to give his animal to drink —
a Jew may give his animal to drink after him,
and if it was for a Jew — it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִילֵּא מַיִם לְהַשְׁקוֹת בְּהֶמְתּוֹ מַשְׁקֶה אַחֲרָיו יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second example of the rule in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water drawn for the גוי's animal may be used. Water drawn for the Jew may not.

steps.title: משנה: A ramp made by a gentile
steps.stepSummary: If a גוי made a ramp to get off a ship, a Jew may go down after him. If it was made for the Jew, it is אסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a גוי made a ramp to go down on, a Jew may go down after him. But if it was for the Jew, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third example of the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building a ramp is a מלאכה. Even so, a Jew may use it if the גוי built it for himself. This sets up the story that follows.

phrases.english: If a gentile made a ramp to go down on —
a Jew may go down after him,
and if it was for a Jew — it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָשָׂה גּוֹי כֶּבֶשׁ לֵירֵד בּוֹ יוֹרֵד אַחֲרָיו יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third example of the same rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew may use a ramp the גוי made for himself, but not one made for the Jew.

steps.title: Story: רבן גמליאל and the זקנים walk down a gentile's ramp
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל and the זקנים were on a ship. A גוי made a ramp to go down, and they went down on it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story with רבן גמליאל and the זקנים, who were traveling on a ship. A גוי made a ramp to go down on it, and רבן גמליאל and the זקנים went down on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה backs up the ramp rule with a real story. Great חכמים used a ramp a גוי had made on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows the rule in practice: since the גוי made the ramp for himself, the חכמים were allowed to use it. It supports step 9.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the story as allowing a ramp made for Jews. It fits the rule only because the גוי made the ramp for his own use. The גמרא will look at this point.
steps.whatToRemember: What matters is who the גוי did the מלאכה for: if for himself, a Jew may benefit. If for the Jew, it is אסור.

phrases.english: There was an incident with Rabban Gamliel and the Elders
who were traveling on a ship
and a gentile made a ramp to go down on it,
and Rabban Gamliel and the Elders went down on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וּזְקֵנִים שֶׁהָיוּ בָּאִין בִּסְפִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that supports the ramp rule in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a Jew may use a ramp a גוי made for himself.
steps.raayaSupportSource: What רבן גמליאל and the זקנים actually did on the ship.

steps.title: Why the lamp case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that we need both the נר case and the מים case. A lamp serves everyone equally. With water, there is a worry that the גוי will draw extra for the Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Both cases were needed. If the משנה had taught only the lamp, I would say it is permitted because one lamp lights for one person as well as for a hundred. But for water, we should make a גזירה, because the גוי might draw extra water for the Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by explaining why it lists both a lamp and water. Each case teaches something the other does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a lamp, the Jew's presence adds no extra work for the גוי, since the same light serves everyone. With water, the גוי could quietly draw more because of the Jew. So we might have thought water should be forbidden. The משנה teaches that water is also permitted when the גוי drew it for himself.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was necessary (to teach every case)
A lamp for one is a lamp for a hundred: no extra work is needed for more people
Let us make a protective rabbinic decree (גזירה)
To add more, to increase the amount

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of נר לאחד נר למאה comes back at the end of this section, in רבא's answer.

phrases.english: GEMARA
And it was necessary
for if it had taught us only a lamp
(I would say it is permitted) because a lamp for one is a lamp for a hundred
but for water, let us decree
lest he come to draw extra for the sake of the Jew

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה's three cases (steps 7 to 10) and explains why the lamp and water cases are both needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lamp and water cases are both needed. A lamp involves no added work for more people, while water could involve added work, so we might have forbidden it.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need the ramp case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the כבש case adds, since it seems to teach nothing new beyond the lamp.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do I need the ramp?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה mentions the ramp at all. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ramp is like a lamp: once it is built, it serves everyone with no extra work. So the lamp case already seems to teach the rule for the ramp.

phrases.english: And why do I need the ramp?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of why each case is needed and turns to the third case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point the ramp case teaches beyond the lamp case.

steps.title: The ramp case brings the story of רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The ramp is mentioned so the משנה can tell the story of רבן גמליאל and the זקנים, which shows the halacha was followed in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us the incident of רבן גמליאל and the זקנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ramp case is there to bring in the story of רבן גמליאל, not to teach a new rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ramp adds no new law. Its value is that great חכמים actually acted on this rule. That is a strong proof that the היתר is the practical הלכה.

phrases.english: the incident of Rabban Gamliel and the Elders
is what it teaches us

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וּזְקֵנִים קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ramp case exists to bring the story of רבן גמליאל, showing the rule was used in practice.

steps.title: ברייתא: grass and water, and the limit when the גוי knows the Jew
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a Jew may use grass or water a גוי gathered for his own animal, but not if it was gathered for the Jew. This applies only when the גוי does not know the Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים taught: If a גוי gathered grass, a Jew may feed his animal after him. If it was for the Jew, it is forbidden. If he drew water to give his animal to drink, a Jew may water his animal after him. If it was for the Jew, it is forbidden. When does this apply? When the גוי does not know him. But if he knows him, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds the case of grass and sets a new limit. The היתר applies only when the גוי does not know the Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the גוי knows the Jew, we assume he probably gathered extra with his Jewish acquaintance in mind. That makes it like work done for the Jew, which is forbidden. The גמרא will challenge this limit later, in step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? (introduces a limit)
He knows him (the גוי is acquainted with the Jew)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two problems coming up. The next challenge (step 15) is about the grass being מוקצה. The later challenge (step 17) is about the 'knows him' limit.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A gentile who gathered grass
a Jew may feed (his animal) after him
and if it was for the Jew, it is forbidden
If he drew water to give his animal to drink
a Jew may water (his animal) after him
and if it was for the Jew, it is forbidden
In what case are these words said?
when he does not know him
but if he knows him, it is forbidden

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that expands the משנה's water case and adds a limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew may benefit from grass or water a גוי gathered for himself, only if the גוי does not know the Jew. If he knows him, it is forbidden.

steps.title: Challenge: the gathered grass is מוקצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from רב הונא in the name of רבי חנינא. One may stand an animal over grass, but not over מוקצה, and grass a גוי picked is מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב הונא said in the name of רבי חנינא: A person may stand his animal over grass on שבת, but not over מוקצה on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions how a Jew may feed his animal the grass the גוי picked. That grass is מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grass still growing in the ground is not a problem, because the animal eats it where it is. Picked grass is מוקצה, and placing the animal over it risks the owner lifting it by hand. So how can the ברייתא say the Jew may feed his animal from it?

keyTerms.meaning: Something set aside that may not be handled on שבת

phrases.english: Is that so?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Huna say in the name of Rabbi Chanina:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲמִיד אָדָם בְּהֶמְתּוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי עֲשָׂבִים בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: A person may stand his animal over grass on Shabbat

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא עַל גַּבֵּי מוּקְצֶה בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: but not over muktzeh on Shabbat

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's permission to feed an animal from the גוי's picked grass.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that a Jew may feed his animal from grass a גוי picked.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Picked grass is מוקצה, and רבי חנינא forbids standing an animal over מוקצה. So feeding from it should be forbidden.

steps.title: Answer: the animal walks to the grass by itself
steps.stepSummary: The Jew only stands the animal in front of the grass at a distance. The animal walks over and eats on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: He stands it in front of the grass, and it goes by itself and eats.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא means the Jew places the animal facing the grass from a distance, and the animal goes and eats by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not mean the Jew puts the animal right over the מוקצה. Because the animal moves to the grass itself, the Jew is not near the grass and there is no worry he will handle it. So the ברייתא does not contradict רבי חנינא.

keyTerms.meaning: He stands it in front of it (at a distance)

phrases.english: He stands it in front of it
and it goes by itself and eats

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means the Jew places his animal right over the picked grass.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Jew stands the animal at a distance facing the grass, and the animal goes to eat on its own, so there is no concern about handling מוקצה.

steps.title: Challenge: the גוי on the ship knew רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the limit that if the גוי knows the Jew it is forbidden. It then asks: the גוי on the ship knew רבן גמליאל, so how could he use the ramp?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: When does this apply? When he does not know him, but if he knows him it is forbidden. But רבן גמליאל was known to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's limit about 'knows him.' It shows a contradiction with the story of רבן גמליאל on the ship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They traveled together on the ship, so the גוי surely knew רבן גמליאל. By the ברייתא's rule, using the ramp should have been forbidden. Yet רבן גמליאל and the זקנים used it.

phrases.english: The Master said:
In what case are these words said? When he does not know him
but if he knows him, it is forbidden
But Rabban Gamliel was known to him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the 'knows him' limit of step 14 and sets it against the story in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that if the גוי knows the Jew, benefit is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The גוי on the ship knew רבן גמליאל, yet רבן גמליאל used the ramp. That seems to contradict the rule.

steps.title: אביי: the ramp was not made in front of him
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the גוי made the ramp when רבן גמליאל was not present, so he made it only for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It was not done in his presence.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction by saying the גוי built the ramp when רבן גמליאל was not there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the Jew is a problem only if the Jew is in mind while the work is being done. If רבן גמליאל was not in front of the גוי at the time, the גוי made the ramp only for himself. In אביי's view, the 'knows him' limit still applies to a ramp.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It was not in his presence

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the גוי knew רבן גמליאל, he made the ramp with him in mind.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ramp was built when רבן גמליאל was not present, so the גוי made it only for himself.

steps.title: רבא: a ramp is like a lamp
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that even if it was done in front of רבן גמליאל, it does not matter. A ramp, like a lamp, serves a hundred people as easily as one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even if you say it was in his presence, a lamp for one is a lamp for a hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer: knowing the Jew does not matter for a ramp at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'knows him' limit applies only where the גוי might do extra work for the Jew, as with grass or water. A ramp, like a lamp, needs no extra work for more people. So even if the גוי knew him and saw him, nothing was added for him.
steps.whatToRemember: A Jew may benefit from work a גוי did for himself, but not work done for the Jew. When the גוי knows the Jew, it is forbidden for things the גוי could make more of, like grass or water. For a lamp or a ramp, which serve everyone the same, רבא says knowing him does not matter. אביי instead explains the ship story as not done in front of רבן גמליאל.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Even if you say it was in his presence
a lamp for one is a lamp for a hundred

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer from אביי to the challenge of step 17, using the principle from step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing categories (no added work versus possible added work)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'knows him' limit applies to every kind of work a גוי does.
steps.terutzMaskana: For things like a lamp or ramp, which serve many with no extra work, knowing the Jew makes no difference.

steps.title: Challenge to רבא from רבן גמליאל's own words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא. רבן גמליאל himself said they could use the ramp because it was made 'not in our presence', which fits אביי's answer and not רבא's.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: רבן גמליאל said to them, 'Since he made it when we were not there, we may go down on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's answer by quoting רבן גמליאל's exact reason for using the ramp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said it would be fine even if the ramp was made in front of רבן גמליאל. But רבן גמליאל's stated reason was 'since it was not in our presence', so being present seems to matter, just as אביי said.

keyTerms.meaning: We will go down on it

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabban Gamliel said to them:
Since he made it not in our presence,
we will go down on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's answer in step 19 and seems to support אביי in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that presence does not matter for a ramp
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן גמליאל's stated reason depends on the ramp being made in his absence, so presence does matter.

steps.title: Reading the quote without 'not in our presence'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers for רבא by fixing the wording. רבן גמליאל really said only, 'Since he made it, we may go down on it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it this way: 'Since he made it, we may go down on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by correcting the text of the quote so it no longer mentions presence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the words 'not in our presence' are taken out, the quote no longer says that presence matters. The reason becomes simply that the ramp was already made, and that fits רבא: a ramp serves many people as easily as one.
steps.confusionAlert: אֵימָא here does not mean the source is being thrown out. The גמרא is fixing the wording of the quote so that it fits רבא's view.

phrases.english: Say:
Since he made it, we will go down on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Text correction (emending the wording of the source)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן גמליאל relied on the ramp being made in his absence.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבן גמליאל relied only on the fact that the ramp was already made, which fits רבא.

steps.title: Challenge from a bathhouse in a mixed city
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that in a city with mostly Jews, one must wait after שבת before using a bathhouse that was heated on שבת. This suggests we worry the work was done for Jews even though no Jew was present.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A city where Jews and גוים live has a bathhouse that is heated and used on שבת. If most people are גוים, a Jew may bathe there right after שבת. If most are Jews, he must wait the time it takes to heat the water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to challenge the idea that work a גוי does when the Jew is not there counts as done for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bathhouse owner did not heat the water in front of any specific Jew, yet a mostly-Jewish city must still wait. That seems to go against אביי's rule that work done away from a Jew is for the גוי himself.

keyTerms.meaning: The amount of time it takes to heat

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A city in which Jews and gentiles live,
and there was a bathhouse in it
that operates on Shabbat,
if the majority are gentiles,
it is permitted to bathe in it immediately (after Shabbat).
If the majority are Jews,
he must wait the time it takes to heat hot water!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 21 settles the wording question, the גמרא tests the אביי and רבא debate with a new source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that work a גוי does away from a Jew is for the גוי himself (אביי)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No Jew was present at the bathhouse, yet a mostly-Jewish city must still wait, so the work is treated as done for Jews.

steps.title: The bathhouse is heated for the majority
steps.stepSummary: The bathhouse case is different. The owner heats the water with the majority of the city in mind, so in a mostly-Jewish city it is heated for Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, when they heat the water, they heat it with the majority in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the challenge by explaining why the bathhouse case is special.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A public bathhouse serves the whole town, so the owner plans the heating for the main group of customers. If most of them are Jews, the heating is for Jews even with no Jew watching. This is a different situation from a private ramp, so the ramp ruling still stands.

phrases.english: There, when they heat,
they heat with the majority in mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (public service aimed at the majority)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bathhouse shows that work done away from Jews still counts as done for them.
steps.terutzMaskana: A public bathhouse is heated for the majority, so it does not challenge the ramp ruling.

steps.title: Challenge from a lamp at a mixed banquet
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a Jew may use a lamp's light at a banquet if most people there are גוים. But the גוי surely knows the Jew at a shared meal, so why is it allowed?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A lamp lit at a banquet. If most people are גוים, a Jew may use its light. If most are Jews, it is forbidden. If it is half and half, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another source to test the rule that if the גוי knows the Jew, it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At a shared banquet the גוי certainly knows the Jew is there. Even so, the ברייתא allows using the light when most people are גוים. That seems to go against the 'knows him' rule from the ברייתא in step 14, which is quoted in step 17.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A lamp lit at a banquet,
if the majority are gentiles,
it is permitted to use its light;
if the majority are Jews, it is forbidden;
half and half, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second test source, following the same pattern as step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that if the גוי knows the Jew, it is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: At a banquet the גוי knows the Jew, yet using the light is allowed when most people are גוים.

steps.title: The lamp is also lit for the majority (answer begins)
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins the same kind of answer: the lamp is also lit with the majority in mind. The sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, when they light it...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer the lamp challenge, using the same idea it used for the bathhouse. The rest of the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word נָמֵי ('also') tells us this answer copies the bathhouse answer. The lamp is lit for the main group at the banquet, so the גוי knowing one Jew does not change who it was lit for.
steps.whatToRemember: In both the bathhouse and the lamp cases, a גוי providing something for a group does it with the majority in mind. So in group settings the majority decides. This does not cancel the ברייתא's 'knows him' rule for an individual Jew.

phrases.english: There too, when they light (it)...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24 by using the same reasoning as step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (lit for the majority); the sentence is incomplete on this amud
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גוי knows the Jew, so the light should be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lamp is lit for the majority, so the majority decides (the answer finishes on the next amud).
